messages.subject: DateTime error
parts:
Jürgen
I am sorry to have to ask for help but I cannot see what is going wrong here.
I have a datetime error for a Reconyx camera.

When I use an image app the DateTime Original field is absent. 
So I believe it is the DateTime error in Reconyx camera.

So I used the fixDateTimeOriginal().  Here is the console output.
> #  fix datetime for old Reconyx cameras
> dir("~/Desktop/CTimg_R/Subset/")
[1] "WGND_EA3712-202110"
> target.dir <- "~/Desktop/CTimg_R/Subset"
> fixDateTimeOriginal(inDir     = target.dir,
+                     recursive = TRUE)
Error: File not found - ~/Desktop/CTimg_R/Subset
running command 'exiftool "-DateTimeOriginal>DateTimeOriginal" -r -overwrite_original -ext JPG "~/Desktop/CTimg_R/Subset"' had status 1
> 

line 2 proves to me that the path is correct and the file does exist 
(There are species subdirectories with images with a  ".JPG" extension)
line 4 is a bit redundant (but I followed the help file) and giving the dir path directly did not help.

So I do not understand the file not found error.

In RStudio I used dir() to convince myself that there is nothing wrong with the path.

I have used the function previously without difficulty.

David

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] DateTime error
parts:
Hi David,

fixDateTimeOriginal() is for situations where the date/time tag was written to the MakerNotes instead of the Exif part of image metadata, and simply copies it over. That happens in a few Reconyx models.

To be sure I'd suggest to check the image metadata and try to find the DateTimeOriginal field. Either use exifTagNames(), or check with a recent version of digiKam which includes ExifTool (right side of the screen "Metadata" tag, then "ExifTool" tag).

In normal images you should see "DateTimeOriginal" in the "Exif" group. If it is absent under "Exif", but present under "MakerNotes", you can fit it with fixDateTimeOriginal(). If it is generally absent (e.g. images downloaded from image sharing websites have their metadata scrubbed), things will get more complicated.

So please let us know if you can find DateTimeOriginal anywhere for those images.

Best regards,

Jürgen
